correctness.rationale: Every subgroup is uniquely parametrized by (U,d,x+U) for d>1 or (U,1) for d=1. For kernel intersection rank r, common complement survives iff affine cosets meet, with exactly p^(n-r) aligned ordered lifts. Gaussian subspace intersection counts give S(k,l,r); summation over disjoint subspaces gives Z(k,d), including whole/trivial exclusions. No unproved infinite extrapolation is used. Standalone exact set-enumeration reproduces seven degree distributions and five complete pairwise meet distributions, including composite complement order.

value.rationale: The joint meet-order distribution is a natural exact invariant of the subgroup lattice for an infinite, structurally coherent family. It determines the entire degree polynomial, edge count and complement-divisor-dependent local degrees; these quantities are not determined by prior connectivity or diameter statements. The distinction between subspace ranks and complement divisor gcds is genuinely structural, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
